title: One thread-safe cache instead of one per service

blocks.text: The page's pitfall is a cache rolled by hand in every service. Its fix is one reusable `ThreadSafeCache<K, V>` that wraps `ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent`:

items: `getOrCompute(key, computeFunction)` returns the cached value for the key, computing it with `computeFunction` on first access only, and returns that same object afterwards. It is **thread-safe by construction**: when two threads ask for a missing key at once, the value is computed **once**, and both threads get the same object. A `null` key or function throws `NullPointerException`. Only the key being computed waits: a different key is computed at the same time;
`get(key)` is the cached value as an `Optional`, empty when there is none;
`invalidate(key)` forgets that key (and only that key), so the next `getOrCompute` computes it again;
`size()` is the number of cached keys.
the first `getOrCompute("user-1001", load)` calls `load`, and a second call returns the same object without calling it;
after `invalidate("user-1001")`, `get("user-1001")` is empty and the next `getOrCompute` calls `load` again;
two threads that both ask for `"order-5000"` while it is being computed see one call of the function between them.

cases.says: A value is computed on first access, reused after, and computed again after invalidate.
Two threads asking for the same missing key at once compute its value once.
invalidate(key) forgets that key only: another cached key keeps its value and is not computed again.
Two different keys are computed at the same time: one key's slow computation does not hold up another key's.

concepts: Thread-safe caching with ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent is encapsulated in one reusable cache that computes each key once.
